Location & Accommodations - e-Fest | Undergraduate Entrepreneurship Competition

# Location & Accommodations

e-Fest is a 3 day celebration of undergraduate student entrepreneurship, culminating in the final championship event of the Schulze Entrepreneurship Challenge. The challenge begins as an online competition. After a selection process, where each submission is reviewed by at least 2 judges, the Top 25 Finalists will be invited to Minneapolis to compete in person for recognition and cash prizes.

Top 25 finalist teams and advisors will receive a stipend to cover airfare, ground transport to/from the airport, hotel accommodations, and incidental expenses, such as snacks.

Finalist Competitors: Please plan to be checked in at the hotel and ready by 5 p.m. on Thursday.

Finalist teams and advisors are responsible for reserving their hotel rooms from a block of rooms set aside for e-Fest. There will be one room allocated for each faculty advisor, and at least one double occupancy room available for every two members on a team.

Questions? Email: e-fest@eix.org

## Apply for a WECode 2026 Scholarship

#### Scholarship applications are OPEN.

We are dedicated to making WECode accessible to everyone. 

Over the past few years, we've been developing efforts to make our conference as inclusive as possible, and we're grateful to all parties that have enabled us to work towards this ongoing initiative. For the 2026 WECode Conference, we are excited to announce that we're expanding our impact and offering a generous scholarship that will help make the in-person WECode experience possible to more prospective attendees.

The WECode 2027 scholarship covers the full cost of the conference ticket priced at our early bird ticket rate, and provides financial aid for travel and other related expenses. This award amount totaling to $200 will go towards your WECode conference ticket purchase AND related transportation expenses (including but not limited to flight cost, additional food, transportation, etc.). 

These scholarships are limited, and will be distributed to those who 

1. are in the most financial need, and 
2. would benefit the most from the in-person conference experience (demonstrated by essay responses).

ATC 2026: The 2026 ACM SIGOPS Annual Technical Conference

# ATC 2026

## ATC 2026 Student Scholarships and Travel Grants

ATC 2026 offers a limited number of grants to help full-time undergraduate and graduate students attend the conference in Hong Kong. Students may apply whether or not they are presenting work.

Funding is competitive and may cover conference registration and part of reasonable travel and accommodation expenses. Awards may not cover all requested costs.

### Eligibility

Applicants must:

- be enrolled full-time at an accredited institution;
- study computer science, computer engineering, or a related field;
- attend ATC 2026 in person if selected; and
- disclose all confirmed or pending funding for the trip.

Postdoctoral researchers are also eligible.

### Application Materials

Please submit:

- the completed application form;
- a CV of no more than two pages;
- proof of current full-time student status.

Applications will be evaluated based on financial need, relevance to ATC, expected benefit from attending, available institutional support, and contributions to broad participation.

title: Hudson River Trading CppCon Scholarship | CppCon
text:
Hudson River Trading CppCon Scholarship | CppCon

# Hudson River Trading CppCon Scholarship

Hudson River Trading’s (HRT) engineering culture is built on rigor, performance, and intellectual honesty. We write code to solve complex, real-time challenges at the intersection of computer science and global markets, and we believe that fostering deep technical expertise, curiosity, and diverse perspectives are essential to advancing the state of modern computing.

As part of this commitment, we are proud to partner with CppCon – the premier forum for the C++ community to share knowledge and explore language evolution – to support the next generation of C++ engineers who are passionate about building high-performance, reliable software. We are supporting CppCon’s mission of providing opportunities for C++ developers, researchers, and language contributors to learn from leading practitioners by offering a scholarship for select students to attend CppCon 2026.

Through this scholarship, we aim to help reduce barriers to attending CppCon and invest in students eager to grow as software engineers and quant researchers. We are looking for students who are not just users of C++, but genuinely curious about what happens “under the hood” – from memory models and concurrency to low-level hardware behavior – and who are excited by challenging problems, motivated by learning, and serious about building excellent software.
